chunks: Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

When a man enters a town, he is a guest of those among its people who share his faith until he departs from them. It is not appropriate for the guest to fast except with their permission, lest they prepare something and it be spoiled. And it is not appropriate for them to fast except with the permission of the guest, lest he feel constrained before them and desire something, then leave it for their sake.

key_terms.أَهْلِ دِينِهِ: those who share his religion, indicating communal religious fellowship
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ ٱلضَّيْفِ: with the guest's permission, indicating reciprocal consideration
key_terms.بِإِذْنِهِمْ: with their permission, indicating regard for the host's circumstances
key_terms.ضَيْفٌ: a guest who is under the care and consideration of others
key_terms.يَحْتَشِمَهُمْ: to feel shy or constrained before them
key_terms.يَشْتَهِيَ: to desire food or something offered
key_terms.يَصُومَ: to fast, here referring to voluntary fasting in a social setting

ai.seo_question: Can a guest or host observe a fast without the other's permission in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the mutual etiquette between a guest and the people hosting him within the community of faith. It gives a ruling related to voluntary fasting, emphasizing consideration, hospitality, and avoiding embarrassment or wasted effort between hosts and guests.
